free_tier.stated: One price of USD 20 per seat per month for 2 vCPU (1 guaranteed, the second when the host has spare capacity), 4 GiB RAM, a 20 GB disk, 100 GB of egress and a public IPv4, with no per-second meter and no overage. Each seat is one box with SSH, an MCP server inside the box and a dashboard. Idle boxes sleep, which is how the flat price is possible.

chaining: A box that keeps its filesystem and runs an MCP server is the piece a stateless sandbox lacks: an agent reconnects over SSH or HTTPS by hostname and finds its tools and caches still installed, so the setup cost is paid once a month rather than once a run.

limits.value: The 100 GB monthly egress and the single guaranteed vCPU are the terms that bind: the second vCPU is best-effort on host spare capacity, and the box sleeps when idle so a background job that needs a warm box has to keep it awake.

the vendor's own comparison at 730 hours per month: AWS t3.medium totals USD 35.62, Google Cloud e2-medium USD 41.15, Azure B2s USD 36.42, list prices read 2026-10-18
one LXC container per agent with real root, a built-in MCP server over stdio, a routable hostname with TLS, and state that survives between runs until the box is deleted
'the box sleeps when idle' and the seat is a share of an instance rather than a dedicated machine

notes: Recorded as paid-only rather than trial-only because no free lane was found on the pages reached. The hosted cloud console at cloud.containarium.dev answered with a login wall behind scripts (broker read reported login-wall, status 409), so a trial, if one exists, is invisible without an account; that is the open question and an account is what would settle it. The core is Apache 2.0 and self-hostable, which is not a price for a user but does mean the same box can run on any rented VM. At USD 20 for 1 guaranteed vCPU and 4 GiB this is the cheapest flat-rate agent box found after RemoteHost's per-hour arithmetic.
